questions.q: Which method of persuasion does the summary call the most persuasive?
a: Logos, because it rests on truth and reason
Pathos, because it moves the audience emotionally
Ethos, because authority silences objections
Humor, because it puts the crowd at ease
questions.why: Lesson 1 rates logos highest because it rests on facts instead of feelings.

questions.q: Why is pathos described as sneaky?
a: It manipulates feelings instead of convincing through facts
It relies on the speaker's reputation rather than evidence
It works only with young audiences
It requires long memorized passages
questions.why: Lesson 1 calls pathos deceitful because it plays on emotions instead of proving a case.

questions.q: Which three qualities help an audience trust a speaker?
a: Intelligence, strong character and goodwill
Confidence, humor and a loud voice
Experience, wealth and famous connections
Sincerity, patience and good looks
questions.why: Lesson 2 says intelligence, character and goodwill are what make an audience see you as trustworthy.

questions.q: In the four-part speech structure, what comes right after the introduction?
a: The narrative, which uses emotion to build your case
The arguments, which prove your points with facts
The conclusion, which summarizes your case
The speaker's credentials and qualifications
questions.why: Lesson 3 puts the narrative second, where pathos awakens emotion before the arguments.

questions.q: What should the conclusion of a speech do?
a: Summarize the points and end with a punchline or emotional bang
Introduce a new argument for the audience to consider
Thank the organizers and list your sources
Repeat the introduction word for word
questions.why: Lesson 3 says to close briefly by summarizing and finishing with a strong line.
